notes: The item card set. See docs/CARD_SET.md for the rules this file follows. Every text and art array is [Prototype, Fine, Masterwork]; a numeric effect param given as a 3-item array is that value per tier. Check with: npm run portfolio. Provisional: nothing here has been playtested, and every number is open to change once the cards are in the real game.

cards.name: Workbench
cards.object: A place to lay your parts out.

text: +1 hand size.
+1 hand size and +1 draw.
+2 hand size and +1 draw.

rules: A fixture: no gadget, so its passive is stronger than a Common's usually is.
art: Two crates with an old door laid across them.
A proper trestle bench with a wooden vice.
A cabinetmaker's bench with a tool rack and brass fittings.

cards.name: Pocket Watch
cards.object: An open-face watch on a fob chain.

text: +2 draws.
+2 draws.
+3 draws.

gadget.name: Stop Time
text: An opponent misses its next turn.
Stopwatch: an opponent misses its next turn, and you get +1 draw this duel.
Repeater: every opponent misses its next turn, and you get +1 draw this duel.

rules: Skipped turns stack: stopping a frozen opponent adds another missed turn.
Masterwork doesn't need a target; Prototype and Fine do.
Replaces the old perGrade 0.2 scaling, which gave 2 turns at Silver while the text said Gold.
art: A tin watch with a wire bow, a cracked dial and a taped case.
A complete watch with a seconds dial and a stopwatch pusher.
An engraved repeater with a skeleton window over the train and a ruby jewel.

cards.name: Glue Pot
cards.object: A pot of hide glue with a brush in the lid.

text: Start each duel with a temporary Duct Tape.
Start each duel with a temporary Duct Tape.
Start each duel with 2 temporary Duct Tapes.

gadget.name: Quick Patch
text: Add a temporary Duct Tape to your hand.
Add a temporary Duct Tape to your hand. It counts as a real part.
Add 2 temporary Duct Tapes to your hand. They count as real parts.

rules: "Counts as a real part" means a meld made only of these tapes and wilds is still legal (it passes requireNaturalInMeld).
The Purist Inspector twist disables these tapes like any other wild. That's the counter to this item.
art: A dented tin can of glue with a stick for a brush.
A stoneware glue pot with a proper brush.
A copper double-boiler glue pot with a spirit burner.

cards.name: Coin Press
cards.object: A screw press for stamping tokens.

text: +2 credits after each duel.
+2 credits after each duel, +1 more for each opponent.
+3 credits after each duel, +1 more for each opponent.

gadget.name: Raise the Stakes
text: You and every opponent each add 1 part of the stake material to the pot.
You add 1 part of the stake material to the pot, and every opponent adds 2.
You add 1 part of the stake material to the pot, and every opponent adds 2 of one material better.

rules: Your added part comes from your parts deck and must meet the stake rule (that material or better); if you lose, it's lost with your stake.
You can't use it without a spare part that meets the stake rule.
The opponents' parts use the duel's stake material, not a random one from their decks (a change from the live version, which also costs you nothing).
art: A bench screw with a bottle cap for a die.
A cast-iron fly press with a weighted arm.
A gilt mint press with engraved dies and a coin tray.

cards.name: Magnifier
cards.object: A reading glass with a handle.

text: Your checks leave 1 fewer possibility (never fewer than 2).
Your checks leave 1 fewer possibility (never fewer than 2). Appraisers charge 1 credit less.
Your checks leave 1 fewer possibility, down to exact. Appraisers charge 1 credit less.

gadget.name: Spyglass
text: In a duel: see every opponent's hand for the rest of it. On a parcel: learn its metal for certain, leaving 1 of 3 numbers.
In a duel: see every opponent's hand for the rest of it. On a parcel: learn its metal for certain, leaving 1 of 2 numbers.
In a duel: see every opponent's hand for the rest of it. On a parcel: unwrap it.

rules: Can't be used in a duel once every hand is already revealed.
The passive also sharpens the Spyglass's own parcel checks.
art: A lens from a pair of spectacles wired to a stick.
A horn-handled reading glass.
A silver-mounted glass with a folding second lens.

cards.name: Sorting Tray
cards.object: A shallow tray with compartments for small parts.

text: +1 hand size and +1 draw.
+1 hand size and +1 draw.
+1 hand size and +2 draws.

gadget.name: Rummage
text: +3 draws this duel.
+4 draws this duel.
+5 draws this duel.

rules: Extra draws only matter in duels you'd otherwise lose on the draw limit; using it early wastes nothing, but using it in a duel you win anyway does.
art: A muffin tin.
A wooden tray with dovetailed compartments.
A mahogany tray with labelled brass-edged compartments.

cards.name: Salvage Rig
cards.object: A grabbing claw on a telescoping pole.

text: +1 credit when you go out.
+2 credits when you go out.
+3 credits when you go out.

gadget.name: Snatch
text: Take a random card from an opponent's hand.
Look at 2 random cards from an opponent's hand and take 1.
Look at an opponent's hand and take any card.

rules: The opponent's hand stays 1 card smaller for the rest of the duel, which makes it harder for it to go out.
The card you take is temporary: it's gone after the duel unless you go out with it, and even then it doesn't join your deck.
art: A litter picker with bent fork tines.
A sprung claw on a wooden pole.
A brass telescoping grab with a pistol grip and three jointed fingers.

cards.name: Spare Reel
cards.object: A fishing reel kept in the kit bag.

text: Start each duel with a temporary Adaptor.
Start each duel with a temporary Adaptor.
Start each duel with a temporary Adaptor and a temporary Duct Tape.

gadget.name: Cast Line
text: Draw 2 cards now.
Draw 3 cards now.
Draw 4 cards now.

rules: These draws don't count against your draw limit.
art: A cotton reel on a nail with string wound round it.
A wooden centrepin reel.
A brass multiplying reel with an ivory handle.

cards.name: Music Box
cards.object: A wind-up cylinder music box.

text: Minions can't take your discards on your first 2 turns of each duel.
Minions can't take your discards on your first 3 turns of each duel.
Minions can't take your discards on your first 4 turns of each duel.

gadget.name: Lullaby
text: Every opponent misses its next turn.
Every opponent misses its next turn. Draw 1 card now.
Every opponent misses its next 2 turns. Draw 1 card now.

rules: "Your first 2 turns" counts your discards: the card you discard on turns 1 and 2 can't be taken by any minion that round of turns.
Overlaps the Masterwork Pocket Watch on purpose: this is the Rare that does it from Tin.
art: A cigar box with a comb from a broken toy and a crank handle.
A walnut box with a brass cylinder and a glass inner lid.
An inlaid box with interchangeable cylinders, bells and a dancing figure.

cards.name: Orrery
cards.object: A clockwork model of the planets.

text: +1 draw for each Clockwork item you own, this one included.
+1 draw for each Clockwork item you own, this one included. +1 hand size.
+1 draw for each Clockwork item you own, this one included. +1 hand size. Your other Clockwork gadgets have +1 charge.

gadget.name: Align the Planets
text: Restore 1 charge to each of your other Clockwork gadgets.
Restore 1 charge to each of your other gadgets.
Restore 2 charges to each of your other Clockwork gadgets and 1 to every other gadget.

rules: Charges never go above a gadget's maximum.
It never restores its own charge.
Build-around: weak with no other Clockwork items, strong with three or more.
art: Marbles on bent wire arms round a light bulb, turned by a hand crank.
A brass orrery on a wooden base with the inner planets geared.
A gilt orrery with every planet and moon geared, a sunburst and an engraved horizon ring.

cards.name: Periscope
cards.object: A folding periscope made of two mirrors in a tube.

text: You can see the top card of your draw pile.
You can see the top card of your draw pile.
You can see the top 2 cards of your draw pile.

gadget.name: Up Periscope
text: Look at the top 3 cards of your draw pile and put them back in any order.
Look at the top 4 cards of your draw pile and put them back in any order.
Look at the top 5 cards of your draw pile. Put any of them on the bottom and the rest back in any order.

rules: Doesn't use a draw. Use it before you draw to set up this turn's card.
art: Two shaving mirrors taped into a cardboard tube.
A tin periscope with a sliding eyepiece.
A brass naval periscope with a crosshair lens and a folding handle.

cards.name: Soldering Iron
cards.object: A copper-bit soldering iron heated on a stove.

text: Your Adaptors can change a part's number and material at once.
Your Adaptors can change a part's number and material at once.
Your Adaptors can change a part's number by up to 2 and its material at once.

gadget.name: Solder
text: A part in your hand becomes any material you choose for the rest of the duel.
A part in your hand becomes any material you choose, and its number goes up or down by 1, for the rest of the duel.
Up to 2 parts in your hand each become any material you choose, and each number goes up or down by 1, for the rest of the duel.

rules: The change lasts for this duel only. The card goes back to normal in your deck afterwards.
Numbers stay within 1 to 10.
Embargo still applies: a part changed into the banned material can't be used.
art: A nail bent into a hook, wired to a wooden peg.
A copper-bit iron with a turned beech handle.
A brass spirit-heated iron with interchangeable bits in a fitted case.

cards.name: Sewing Kit
cards.object: A roll-up housewife of needles, thread and pins.

text: The first piece you put on a page after each win counts as 2 pieces.
The first piece you put on a page after each win counts as 2 pieces.
The first 2 pieces you put on pages after each win each count as 2 pieces.

gadget.name: Stitch
text: Move up to 2 pieces of one material from one page to another.
Move up to 3 pieces of one material from one page to another.
Move up to 4 pieces from one page to another. Each lands on the best stage it can fill.

rules: Pieces can only come off an unfinished stage, so no item ever loses a grade.
Moving pieces can finish a stage, which brings that item to life or raises it as usual.
A doubled piece that overfills a stage doesn't carry over.
art: Needles stuck in a cork with thread wound on a lolly stick.
A canvas roll with pockets, a thimble and a bodkin.
A tortoiseshell étui with silver scissors, needle case and a thimble.

cards.name: Thimble
cards.object: A dimpled thimble.

text: Tin pieces count as 2 pieces on Tin stages.
Tin and Wood pieces count as 2 pieces on their own stages.
Tin, Wood and Iron pieces count as 2 pieces on their own stages.

gadget.name: Darn
text: Put 1 part from your parts deck onto a page.
Put up to 2 parts from your parts deck onto pages.
Put up to 3 parts from your parts deck onto pages.

rules: The part leaves your deck for good.
You can't take your deck below 30 parts this way.
Placement follows the normal rule: its own stage, or the best lower stage still open.
art: A bottle cap with dents punched in it.
A brass thimble with an engraved band.
A gold thimble with a moonstone top and a garland border.

cards.name: Brass Scales
cards.object: A pair of balance scales with a set of weights.

text: You can match a stake with parts one material below what's asked.
You can match a stake with parts one material below what's asked.
You can match a stake with parts up to two materials below what's asked.

gadget.name: Weigh In
text: If you lose this duel, your stake comes back to your deck.
If you lose this duel, your stake comes back to your deck. If you win, +3 credits.
If you lose this duel, your stake comes back to your deck. If you win, +3 credits. You can also use it after losing.

rules: Against a boss, you still lose a life.
Using it more than once in a duel does nothing extra; the UI blocks the second use.
On the result screen (Masterwork), it's only offered when you lost.
art: Two tin lids hung from a coat hanger.
Brass pan scales on a wooden base with a box of weights.
An assayer's balance in a glass case, with gilt pans and a vernier pointer.

cards.name: Abacus
cards.object: A bead frame for sums.

text: Parts you sell are worth 1 more credit.
Parts you sell are worth 1 more credit.
Parts you sell are worth 2 more credits.

gadget.name: Haggle
text: Your next purchase in this shop costs 2 less (never below 1).
Your next purchase in this shop costs 3 less (never below 1).
Every purchase in this shop costs 2 less for the rest of this visit (never below 1).

rules: The discount applies to shop slots only, not to rerolls or recharges.
art: Buttons threaded on wires across a picture frame.
A beech abacus with boxwood beads.
An ebony counting frame with ivory beads and brass corner plates.

cards.name: Crowbar
cards.object: A forged pry bar.

text: +1 credit for each parcel you leave behind in a lot you won.
+1 credit for each parcel you leave behind in a lot you won.
+2 credits for each parcel you leave behind in a lot you won.

gadget.name: Prise Open
text: Pick 1 more parcel from a lot you've won.
Pick 1 more parcel from a lot you've won, after seeing the metal of every parcel you didn't pick.
Pick 2 more parcels from a lot you've won.

rules: Use it on the pick screen. Fine lets you use it after opening your picks, so you choose with more known.
The passive counts the parcels left after any extra picks, so the two pull against each other.
art: A bent tent peg.
A forged steel crowbar with a split claw.
A brass-ferruled jemmy in a leather holster, with a hallmark.

cards.name: Horseshoe Magnet
cards.object: A red-painted horseshoe magnet.

text: You can see the top 3 cards of the discard pile.
You can see the top 4 cards of the discard pile.
You can see the top 5 cards of the discard pile.

gadget.name: Pull
text: Instead of drawing, take any card from the discard pile.
Take any card from the discard pile. It doesn't use your draw.
Take any 2 cards from the discard pile, then discard 1. It doesn't use your draw.

rules: The Locked Skip twist (no discard pile draws) blocks Pull too.
Prototype must be used in your draw step and counts as your draw for the turn.
art: A magnet pulled from a speaker, tied to string.
A red-and-silver horseshoe magnet with a keeper bar.
A compound bar magnet of polished lodestone in a gilt cradle.

cards.name: Mousetrap
cards.object: A spring-bar mousetrap.

text: +1 credit whenever a minion takes a card you discarded.
+1 credit whenever a minion takes a card you discarded.
+2 credits whenever a minion takes a card you discarded.

gadget.name: Spring the Trap
text: Set a trap. The next card an opponent takes from the discard pile comes to your hand instead, and that opponent draws from its own pile.
Set a trap. The next card an opponent takes from the discard pile comes to your hand instead, and that opponent gets no card that turn.
Set a trap that catches twice. Each card an opponent takes from the discard pile comes to your hand instead, and that opponent gets no card that turn.

rules: The trap stays set until it catches something or the duel ends; an unsprung trap still uses the charge.
Only one trap can be set at a time.
An opponent with no card that turn still discards, so its hand shrinks by 1.
art: A clothes peg and a lolly stick on a scrap of board.
A sprung wooden trap with a wire bar.
A cast-iron 'Little Nipper' with a brass treadle, mounted like a trophy.

cards.name: Bellows
cards.object: Fireside bellows.

text: +1 draw in duels against a greedy minion.
+1 draw in duels against a greedy minion.
+2 draws in duels against a greedy minion.

gadget.name: Clear the Air
text: Blow the whole discard pile out of this duel.
Take the top card of the discard pile, then blow the rest out of this duel.
Take the top card of the discard pile, then blow the rest out of this duel. +1 credit for each card blown out (up to 5).

rules: Blown-out cards are gone for this duel only. Your own parts are still in your deck afterwards.
Fewer cards in the discard pile means a smaller reshuffle if any draw pile runs out.
Greedy minions now: Magpie, Steam Hound, Boiler Titan, Clockwork King.
art: A hot-water bottle with a pen tube for a nozzle.
Elm-and-leather fireside bellows.
Carved oak bellows with a brass nozzle and studded hide.

cards.name: Oil Can
cards.object: A thumb-pump oil can.

text: You can see each boss's twist on the map from the start of the act.
You can see each boss's twist on the map from the start of the act.
You can see each boss's twist on the map from the start of the act.

gadget.name: Free It Up
text: Boss duels only: switch off a random twist for the rest of the duel.
Boss duels only: switch off a twist of your choice for the rest of the duel.
Boss duels only: switch off every twist for the rest of the duel, and get +2 draws.

rules: With one twist per boss (config.duel.bossTwists = 1), Prototype and Fine do the same thing; they differ once bosses get more twists.
The passive needs boss twists to be rolled when the map is made instead of when the duel starts.
When a twist is switched off, the duel's rules are worked out again without it, so wilds blocked by the Purist Inspector work at once.
art: A washing-up liquid bottle with a bent straw.
A tin thumb-pump oil can with a long spout.
A brass engineer's oiler with a sight glass and a chased lid.

cards.name: Clockwork Mouse
cards.object: A wind-up tin mouse.

text: At the start of each duel, see 1 random card in each opponent's hand.
At the start of each duel, see 2 random cards in each opponent's hand.
At the start of each duel, see 3 random cards in each opponent's hand.

gadget.name: Scamper
text: An opponent drops a random card from its hand onto the discard pile.
Look at an opponent's hand and choose a card for it to drop onto the discard pile.
Look at an opponent's hand and choose 2 cards for it to drop onto the discard pile.

rules: Use it before your draw to take the dropped card this turn. Otherwise the next opponent may take it.
The opponent doesn't draw a replacement, so its hand shrinks.
Peeked cards stay visible until they leave the opponent's hand.
art: A clothes peg with a key glued on and bottle-top wheels.
A lithographed tin mouse with a wind-up key.
A silver automaton mouse with garnet eyes, jointed tail and a fusee movement.

cards.name: Kaleidoscope
cards.object: A brass-tube kaleidoscope.

text: Your first draw each duel shows you 2 cards. Keep 1; the other goes to the bottom of your draw pile.
Your first 2 draws each duel each show you 2 cards. Keep 1; the other goes to the bottom of your draw pile.
Your first 3 draws each duel each show you 2 cards. Keep 1; the other goes to the bottom of your draw pile.

gadget.name: Turn the Tube
text: Shuffle your hand into your draw pile and draw the same number of cards.
Keep 1 card, shuffle the rest of your hand into your draw pile, and draw back up.
Keep up to 3 cards, shuffle the rest of your hand into your draw pile, and draw back up.

rules: Neither the passive nor the gadget uses extra draws from your limit.
Only draws from your draw pile trigger the passive, not draws from the discard pile.
Temporary cards shuffled back in can be drawn again this duel.
art: A kitchen-roll tube with sweet wrappers and a marble.
A brass tube kaleidoscope with a glass object cell.
A parlour kaleidoscope on a mahogany stand with twin wheels of cut glass.

cards.name: Chess Automaton
cards.object: A cabinet automaton that plays chess.

text: The first time each duel an opponent would go out, it doesn't: it discards a random card instead.
The first time each duel an opponent would go out, it doesn't: it discards a random card instead.
The first 2 times each duel an opponent would go out, it doesn't: it discards a random card instead.

gadget.name: Swap Boards
text: Swap hands with an opponent.
Look at an opponent's hand, then swap hands with it or put it back (the charge is only used if you swap).
Look at an opponent's hand, then swap hands with it or put it back. If you swap, it misses its next turn.

rules: Hands may be different sizes; each side keeps what it's given.
Cards you get from an opponent are temporary: they're gone after the duel and never join your deck.
Your own parts given to the opponent are still in your deck after the duel.
The blocked opponent discards one of its cards at random, not necessarily the one it drew.
art: A cardboard box with a sock-puppet arm and a draughts board.
A painted cabinet with a turbaned figure and a carved chessboard.
A gilt and ebony cabinet with doors open on the gearing and a pearl chess set.

cards.name: Pocket Compass
cards.object: A hinged brass pocket compass.

text: Shops stock 1 extra check card.
Shops stock 1 extra check card. Appraisers charge 1 credit less.
Shops stock 2 extra check cards. Appraisers charge 1 credit less.

gadget.name: Reroute
text: Your next move can go to any stop in the next row, not only a linked one.
Your next move can go to any stop in the next row, not only a linked one.
Your next move can go to any stop up to 2 rows ahead, skipping the row between.

rules: You can't jump into or past the boss's row; you reach the boss from the row before it as normal.
After a reroute, the map's normal links carry on from the stop you landed on.
Fine only improves the passive; its gadget is the same as Prototype's.
art: A magnetised needle floating on a cork in a jam-jar lid.
A brass hunter-case compass with a card dial.
A gilt surveyor's compass with a sighting vane and an engraved rose.

cards.name: Hip Flask
cards.object: A curved pocket flask.

text: +1 draw in boss duels.
+2 draws in boss duels.
+2 draws and +1 hand size in boss duels.

gadget.name: Dutch Courage
text: Boss duels only: if you lose this duel, you don't lose a life. You still lose your stake.
Boss duels only: if you lose this duel, you don't lose a life. You still lose your stake. +2 draws now.
Boss duels only: if you lose this duel, you don't lose a life. You still lose your stake. +2 draws now. You can also use it after losing.

rules: Only one use counts per duel; a second use does nothing and the UI blocks it.
On the result screen (Masterwork), it's only offered after losing a boss duel, and the +2 draws don't apply.
art: A medicine bottle in a sock with a cork.
A pewter flask in a leather wrap.
A silver flask with a bayonet cap, an engraved crest and a gilt cup.
